name: agentic-eclipse-library
description: Process total solar eclipse photos locally: calibrated HDR stacking, corona filter layers, layered Photoshop files, polar views, motion analysis and coronagraph comparisons, with measured inputs and explicit validation limits.

interface.longDescription:
Turn total solar eclipse photographs into linear stacks, corona filter layers, layered Photoshop files and polar views. Explore changes during totality with motion controls, or compare your observations with K-Cor, SOHO/LASCO and SDO/AIA.

Seven guided workflows help you inspect the files, measure calibration and registration, diagnose artefacts at their source and preserve the originals. A case workflow contributed by Raúl Hussein separates photographic acceptance from scientific qualification. The bundled AEL 1.3.4 engine runs numerical processing on your computer. Start with your own observations or a clearly labelled synthetic demonstration. Ask in your preferred language.

Desktop execution and Python 3.10+ are required; Python dependencies are installed separately. Photoshop is optional. Measured calibration and geometry are required: this is not a one-click RAW-to-finished-photo service. Known limitations include ACHF/WOW edge bands, rings of the default WOW next to a lunar limb that the data reach, and some fine-detail sign inversion in WOW bilateral. Passing tests does not validate a new astronomical observation. Missing data stays missing.

Open-source software by Pere Guerra Serra, MIT licensed. The plugin itself has no telemetry or upload service; the AI host's data policies still apply.
capabilities: Corona filter layers and Photoshop files
Whole case to an accepted editable master
defaultPrompt: Help me process my eclipse photos while preserving the originals.
Find what caused the rings in my corona image.
Show me a labelled synthetic eclipse demonstration.

publication.release_notes: Adds a seventh workflow, eclipse-astrophotography, contributed by Raúl Hussein: a whole eclipse case, from the chosen frames to an editable master the photographer accepts, with photographic acceptance kept apart from scientific claims. Also bundles his three-camera case study, the corrected NRGF description in the field lessons and AEL's rule that each optic is corrected before fusing. Bundles AEL 1.3.3, whose numerical code is unchanged from 1.3.2.

ca-ES.subtitle: Processa fotos d’eclipsis
ca-ES.description: Processa fotografies d’eclipsis totals de Sol amb set guies: calibratge i apilat lineal, filtres de la corona, fitxers de Photoshop amb capes, diagnosi d’artefactes, vistes polars i moviment, comparació amb coronògrafs, i un cas sencer, de les fotos triades fins a un màster editable que accepta el fotògraf (guia aportada per Raúl Hussein). Conserva els originals i deixa sense dada allà on no n’hi ha. Inclou una demostració sintètica identificada com a tal. Necessita execució local, Python 3.10 o posterior i dependències addicionals. Els filtres tenen limitacions documentades; les proves del programa no validen una observació nova. Programari lliure de Pere Guerra Serra, amb llicència MIT.

es-ES.subtitle: Procesa fotos de eclipses
es-ES.description: Procesa fotografías de eclipses totales de Sol con siete guías: calibración y apilado lineal, filtros de la corona, archivos Photoshop con capas, diagnóstico de artefactos, vistas polares y movimiento, comparación con coronógrafos, y un caso completo, de las fotos elegidas a un máster editable que acepta el fotógrafo (guía aportada por Raúl Hussein). Conserva los originales y no inventa datos ausentes. Incluye una demostración sintética identificada como tal. Requiere ejecución local, Python 3.10 o posterior y dependencias adicionales. Los filtros tienen limitaciones documentadas; las pruebas del programa no validan una observación nueva. Software libre de Pere Guerra Serra, licencia MIT.

fr-FR.subtitle: Traitez vos photos d’éclipse
fr-FR.description: Traitez des photographies d’éclipses totales de Soleil : calibration et empilement linéaire, filtres de la couronne, fichiers Photoshop avec calques, diagnostic des artefacts, vues polaires, mouvements, comparaisons avec des coronographes et un cas complet, des images choisies à un fichier maître modifiable accepté par le photographe (guide proposé par Raúl Hussein). Préserve les originaux et ne remplace pas les données manquantes. Inclut une démonstration synthétique clairement identifiée. Exécution locale, Python 3.10 ou ultérieur et dépendances supplémentaires requis. Les limites des filtres sont documentées ; les tests du logiciel ne valident pas une nouvelle observation. Logiciel libre de Pere Guerra Serra, licence MIT.
